hypothesis: The core accepted stack's chop-regime sensitivity is unmeasured: exp-20260615-019 only regime-attributed the FGRS sleeve plus one scout, so a portfolio-level chop down-tilt cannot be credibly proposed without knowing whether the core book itself loses in directionless chop or whether chop-loss is sleeve-specific.
changed_variable: read-only entry-day regime_chop_state attribution of the canonical core accepted-stack trades across all three fixed windows
method: For all 61 trades in the canonical core baseline (exp-20260602-003, per-window after.json) across late_strong/mid_weak/old_thin, recompute the entry-day regime via quant/regime_chop_state.py:regime_chop_from_spy_universe at full fidelity (SPY trend/momentum/drawdown/vol + universe breadth above 50d SMA + index agreement), strictly PIT (bars <= entry_date). Bucket realized PnL by regime label; compute Spearman(p_choppy, pnl), Spearman(exposure_scalar, pnl), and the counterfactual of applying the shared exposure_scalar soft tilt. All 61 resolved at full fidelity (stress_confident=true).
interpretation: The core accepted stack does NOT lose in chop: chop-bucket mean PnL is +$2,991 (positive) and Spearman(p_choppy, pnl) is +0.116 pooled and positive in all three windows -- the opposite sign of the FGRS sleeve (-0.324). The core enters in chop only 10% of the time because its entry gates already concentrate entries in trend regimes. Applying the regime_chop_state soft down-tilt to the whole core book would have cut core PnL by -$29,048 (~12%). Conclusion: chop-sensitivity is sleeve-specific, not portfolio-wide. A portfolio-level chop tilt must be scoped to the default-off sleeves with individually-negative Spearman(p_choppy, pnl), never the core stack, and validated on forward entry-regime-tagged rows -- not by re-slicing these frozen windows. Caveat: chop-bucket N is small (6 core trades); direction is robust across windows, magnitude is indicative.

production_impact.parity_note: Read-only replay attribution of the canonical core baseline. No order/ranking/sizing/exit/Gate-4 change.
